main_text.head: PRÆLUDIUM.
AD CAP. III: 1-3. a.
EXPOSITIO TEXTUALIS.

p.i: Verf. 2. Jehovah ! audivi auditionem tuam, & timui : Jehovah ! molitio tua est vita ejus in medio annorum : in medio annorum notifices ; in irâ miserari recorderis.

main_text.p: §. 1. ANsa, quæ Prophetæ sequentem expressit supplicationem, exponitur primo hujus versus colo ; quo propheta ad Jehovam defert, quid oraculum antecedens in animo suo effecerit. De antecedente suâ perceptione dicit, audivi auditionem tuam : Conf. Obad. verf. 1. Verbum cum voce suæ derivationis construction censetur inter elegantias Hebraicæ linguæ. Audire auditionem notat audire auribus, & mente percipere, quicquid de aliquo subjecto dicebatur ; & ad audiendum promulgabatur. Quæ proximè ad Prophetæ institutionem, sed quasi in publico foro de Deo judice dixerat Spiritus Sanctus, se cum attentione animi audivisse profitetur. Verùm consequens istius apud animum suum fuisse notat timorem & consternationem quandam ; addit enim & timui. Timor est passio animi ex perceptione,

page.notes: The initial "A" is a large woodcut letter, printed as "ANsa" in the transcription above; the likely reading is "Ansa" with the initial decorative. Show-through from the reverse side is visible in the title area and was excluded. The text runs to the bottom of the page; there is no catchword, signature or footnote. Line "in irâ miserari recorderis." is printed with the closing period as shown. The word "ptione," at the end is a line-end break of "perceptione," and the hyphen is not printed, so the word is written whole in the paragraph. Faint ink marks in the margins are not text.
